paraphrase: The Buddha makes countless lotuses appear in the sky, each holding a seated buddha; the petals wither and the buddhas are revealed. So, he says, with the buddha-eye he sees that all beings, amid greed, anger and delusion, have within them the Tathāgata's knowledge, eyes and body, seated in meditation, unmoving; though they wander in defilements, the tathāgatagarbha is unstained, full of virtues, no different from his own.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. T666 (vol. 16) not local; from memory.

paraphrase: Nine similes for the tathāgatagarbha hidden in defilements: a buddha inside a withered lotus; honey surrounded by a swarm of bees; a kernel within its husk; gold fallen into a pit of filth; a treasure buried under a poor man's house; a seed inside a fruit that will grow into a great tree; a golden image wrapped in rags left on the road; a poor, ugly woman carrying in her womb a future universal monarch; a golden statue inside a blackened clay mould.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

paraphrase: Whether or not buddhas appear in the world, the tathāgatagarbha of all beings is eternally unchanging; the buddhas teach so that beings may remove their defilements and reveal it.
